How serious can a breach of arcane financial regulations be, really? Just how damning can accountancy be? Even after Friday’s revelation that Manchester City had been found guilty of all but one of the charges brought against them by the Premier League, it was perhaps difficult to grasp the scale of what that meant. After the publication of the independent commission’s findings, there can be no doubt: the commission found that Manchester City cheated, that they did so deliberately, and that they have sought to cover that up with a campaign of…

Speaking about the show in a statement, Deal said: "I invited myself! That’s how I came to play Nobody Loves You More at the Barbican. Years ago, I had worked with Chris Sharp at the 4AD label and I knew...

quietus.title: Gash – At Least You Know What You’re Laughing At
quietus.description: Gash At Least You Know What You’re Laughing At Wisconsin band shape up, think big and get clean at least you know what you're laughing at by gash Wisconsin natives Gash are equal parts brisk and bold. It’s very much in line, sonically, with their previous output, equipped with the same angular, do-it-yourselfness of 304/62, their last album. This record seems less reliant on samplework as a melodic element and more so as a textural one. There’s a warm, roomy quality to a great deal of these tracks, and where guitar and bass might’ve been “lost to the lo-fi”, so to speak, on 304/62, they’re placed front and centre here. Which means that, as slacker rock goes, they exist in a space alongside…

It was also extremely timely, as 2026 is proving to be a vintage year for Occitan music. In fact, several of my favourite French releases of the…

quietus.title: Real Wild Man: Iggy Pop’s Blah Blah Blah at 40
quietus.description: Hitting its 40th anniversary, Julian Marszalek reckons that not only is Iggy Pop’s seventh solo record the most misunderstood of all of his LPs, but that it also happens to be David Bowie’s best album of the 80s Well, no one saw this one coming. Having spent the previous decade lauded as rock & roll’s most compelling survivor – an intoxicating mix of self-destruction, self-sabotage and musical innovation – Iggy Pop found himself, improbably, with a hit album on his hands. Not a reissue, not a compilation or a soundtrack, mind, but a bona fide triumph that would go on to be his most commercially successful album. And if that wasn’t enough, he then ram-raided – for the first and only...

Del Naja can be heard responding: "I don't recognise the offence, though, because under UK law,…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Future Sounds Of Jazz Vol. 16
aquariumdrunkard.description: Future Sounds of Jazz Vol. 16 is both a forecast and a wormhole. Across two discs, Michael Reinboth and Michael Rütten move through jazz, dub, electronic music, improvisation, and psychedelia with the intuitive logic of a late-night DJ set. The result is a strange, elastic universe of DJ Oil, Bitchin Bajas, Booker Stardrum, Nico Zam, Ilhan Ersahin, and Momoko Gill—and a reminder that the future of jazz remains gloriously undefined.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Protomartyr :: Hotel Usona
aquariumdrunkard.description: Protomartyr’s seventh album Hotel Usona (short for United States of North America) creates a fitting soundtrack as the country is pummeled by bad reviews. The Detroit veteran band envisions their homeland as a decrepit hotel where one of the TV channels is a live feed from Trump-Kennedy Center. The hotel is coincidentally located in Anacita, a fictional coastal town created by Casey for 2017’s Relatives in Descent. It’s the kind of place where the “liberal-minded close their eyes and dream of technology and kombucha.”

aquariumdrunkard.title: Lee Ranaldo :: Guitar-Centric Film Soundtracks
aquariumdrunkard.description: As a member of Sonic Youth, Drift, and his many other musical detours, Lee Ranaldo has treated the guitar as a pure sound source, creating dynamic new expressions in rock & roll and the avant-garde alike. But Ranaldo's new project, a soundtrack to director Joris Postema’s "eco-doc" The System, presents a new side of Lee, that of a filmic composer. To commemorate the album's release, Ranaldo sent over notes about nine other guitar-centric soundtracks that serve as conceptual inspirations for The System.

aquariumdrunkard.title: The Aquarium Drunkard Guide to Across the Horizon
aquariumdrunkard.description: What, exactly, is Across the Horizon? It could be accurately described as a podcast, a radio show, an imprint or even a genre; it’s also resulted in a host of compelling collaborations and a series of songs that push at the boundaries of what could be considered ambient music. "It’s like watching a musical community grow in real time," says Bob Holmes. Here’s a look at 10 standout songs from Across the Horizon thus far — music that demonstrates the breadth of the series as a whole.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Dungen :: Vidrig Vår
aquariumdrunkard.description: On the veteran Swedish outfit's most pared down and elegant affair, Vidrig Vår showcases Dungen still operating on a psychedelic wavelength not found elsewhere. Built around bandleader Gustav Ejste's panoramic piano progressions, the ballad-centric record flows with the weightless springtime atmosphere of the band's organically cinematic orbit.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Asher White :: Love Aggregates
aquariumdrunkard.description: Asher White goes maximalist on Love Aggregates , building heavy doses of orchestral power pop from her bedroom. A fragmentary heartbreak album touching on dysphoria, precarious labor, Jerry Garcia, Citi Bikes, and Flatbush in the snow, it transforms intimate falsettos, arpeggiating guitars, and toy piano melodies into a luminous, redemptive vision of love.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Those Were the Days of Miracle and Wonder :: Paul Simon’s Graceland at 40
aquariumdrunkard.description: Paul Simon’s 1986 album Graceland exists in this weird state, an album that eternally evokes 1986, but always sounds so different from other albums of its era. It’s an collection that’s self absorbed, but also so relatable when the listener finds themselves hitting middle age. It brought world music to the forefront, but also presented a misleading picture. It’s a fascinating study in contrast and now, some 40 years later it’s an album we still can’t make up our minds about even as we listen to it for the hundredth time.
